sources.name: Homestead Exemptions by State and Territory - Asset Protection Planners

Tex. Const. Art. XVI, Secs. 50-51; Tex. Prop. Code Secs. 41.001-002. Unlimited homestead exemption: 100 acres rural (single), 200 acres rural (family), 1 acre urban. Sale proceeds exempt 6 months; renting allowed if no other home acquired. Must file homestead declaration. Cap …

Fla. Stat. Ann. Secs. 222.01, 222.02; Fla. Const. Art. X, Sec. 4. Unlimited homestead exemption for an owner-occupied residence, including mobile or modular homes, limited to 0.5 acre in a municipality or 160 acres elsewhere. Spouse or child of a deceased owner may claim the e…

N.Y. Civ. Prac. L. & R. Sec. 5206(a). Homestead exemption for real property, including co-op, condo, or mobile home: $165,550 in Kings, New York, Queens, Bronx, Richmond, Nassau, Suffolk, Rockland, Westchester, and Putnam; $131,325 in Dutchess, Albany, Columbia, Orange, Sarato…
N.J. Stat. Ann. Sec. 2A:61-1. No general homestead exemption; however, property held as tenancy by the entirety is exempt from creditors of a single spouse.

Ill. Comp. Stat. Secs. 5/12-901, 5/12-906. Homestead exemption up to $15,000 for real or personal property, including a farm, lot, buildings, condo, co-op, or mobile home; sale proceeds exempt for one year.
Ohio Rev. Code Ann. Sec. 2329.66(A)(1). Homestead exemption for real or personal property used as a residence.

Ga. Code Ann. Secs. 44-13-100(a)(1), (a)(6); 44-13-1. Homestead exemption up to $21,500 for an owner-occupied residence, including a co-op; $43,000 if married and the property is solely owned by one spouse. Up to $5,000 of unused homestead may be applied to other property.

N.C. Gen. Stat. Sec. 1C-1601(a)(1). Homestead exemption up to $35,000 for an owner-occupied residence, including co-ops; $60,000 if age 65+ and spouse is deceased. Up to $5,000 of unused exemption may be applied to other property.

Mich. Comp. Laws Ann. Sec. 600.5451(n). Homestead exemption $30,000; $45,000 if age 65+ or disabled. Limited to 1 lot in a town, village, or city, or 40 acres elsewhere. Spouse or children of a deceased owner may claim the exemption.
N.J. Stat. Ann. Sec. 2A:61-1. No general homestead exemption; survivorship interest of a spouse in property held as tenancy by the entirety is exempt from creditors of a single spouse.

Va. Code Ann. Sec. 34-4. Homestead exemption $5,000 plus $500 per dependent; $10,000 if age 65+. Includes rents, profits, and sale proceeds up to $5,000. Husband and wife may double; unused portion may apply to personal property. Must file homestead declaration before bankruptcy.
Wash. Rev. Code Sec. 6.13.030. Homestead exemption is the greater of $125,000 or the county median single-family home price. No exemption if subject to a state tax judgment on retirement benefits.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. Sec. 33-1101A and the Predatory Debt Collection Protection Act (Nov. 2022). Homestead exemption up to $400,000 in equity; adjusted annually for CPI starting Jan 1, 2024. Applies to owner-occupied real property, apartments, or mobile homes; sale proceeds exempt…
Tenn. Code Ann. Sec. 26-2-301. Homestead exemption: $7,500 unmarried; $12,500 unmarried age 62+; $20,000 married with one spouse 62+; $25,000 married with both spouses 62+.
Mass. Gen. L. Ch. 188, Secs. 1, 1A. Homestead exemption up to $500,000; $500,000 for each person age 62+ or disabled. Must record a Declaration of Homestead with the county Registry of Deeds.

Ind. Code Ann. Sec. 34-55-10-2(b)(1). Unlimited homestead exemption for real or personal property used as a residence. Property held as tenancy by the entirety may be exempt against debts of only one spouse.
Mo. Ann. Stat. Sec. 513.475. Homestead exemption up to $5,000 for a mobile home.

Md. Courts & Jud. Proc. Code Sec. 11-504. Homestead exemption up to $22,975 for owner-occupied residential property, condo, or co-op. Property held as tenancy by the entirety is exempt against debts of only one spouse.

Colo. Rev. Stat. Sec. 38-41-201. Homestead exemption up to $250,000 for an owner-occupied residence; $350,000 if the owner, spouse, or dependent is age 60 or older or disabled. Sale proceeds are exempt for two years after receipt.
Wisc. Stat. Sec. 815.20. Homestead exemption for property you occupy or intend to occupy; sale proceeds exempt for two years if purchasing another home.
Minn. Rev. Stat. Ann. Sec. 510.02. Homestead exemption up to $450,000; $1,125,000 if used primarily for agriculture. Limited to 0.5 acre in a city or 160 acres elsewhere.
S.C. Code Ann. Sec. 15-41-30(1). Homestead exemption for real property, including co-ops.
Ala. Code § 6-10-2, 27-14-29. Real property or mobile home to $15,000; property cannot exceed 160 acres.
Ky. Rev. Stat. Ann. Sec. 427.060. Unlimited homestead exemption for real or personal property used as a residence.

La. Rev. Stat. Ann. Sec. 20:1; La. Const. Art. 12:9. Homestead exemption up to $35,000 for occupied property; if debt results from catastrophic or terminal illness/injury, exemption is full property value as of one year before filing. Limited to 5 acres in a city/town or 200 a…

Or. Rev. Stat. Sec. 18.395. Homestead exemption up to $40,000 ($50,000 for joint owners) for an owner-occupied or intended residence, including mobile homes or houseboats; limited to 1 block in a city/town or 160 acres elsewhere. Sale proceeds exempt for one year if purchasing…

31 Okla. St. Ann. Sec. 2. Unlimited homestead exemption for up to 160 acres in rural areas or 1 acre in urban areas. Limited to $5,000 if over 25% of property is used for business. Renting the homestead is allowed if no other residence is acquired.

Conn. Gen. Stat. Sec. 52-352b(t). Homestead exemption up to $75,000 for an owner-occupied residence; $125,000 for hospital service judgments. Applies to claims after 1993. Spouses may double the exemption.
Utah Code Ann. Sec. 78-23-3. Homestead exemption up to $30,000 for real property, mobile home, or water rights if primary residence; $5,000 if not primary residence.
Nev. Rev. Stat. Sec. 21.090(1)(l). Homestead exemption up to $550,000 for an owner-occupied residence or mobile home. Homestead declaration must be recorded before filing for bankruptcy.
Iowa Code Ann. Sec. 561.16. Unlimited homestead exemption for up to 40 acres in rural areas or 0.5 acre in urban areas; protection continues despite annexation.

Ark. Const. art. 4. Married persons or heads of household may claim an unlimited homestead exemption on a residence up to 0.25 acre in a city or 80 acres elsewhere; larger homesteads up to 1 acre in a city or 160 acres elsewhere are capped at $2,500. The exemption is not lost …
Kan. Stat. Ann. Sec. 60-2301. Unlimited homestead exemption for up to 160 acres in rural areas or 1 acre in urban areas.

Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 85-3-21. Homestead exemption up to $75,000 for 160 acres; sale proceeds exempt. Mobile home (personal property) up to $30,000; mobile home does not qualify as homestead unless land is owned.
N.M. Stat. Ann. Sec. 42-10-9. Homestead exemption for real property or mobile home; joint owners may double the exemption.
Idaho Code Sec. 50-1003. Homestead exemption up to $100,000 for real property or a mobile home; sale proceeds are exempt for six months.
Neb. Rev. Stat. Secs. 40-101 to 40-108. Homestead exemption limited to head of household; up to 2 lots in a city or village, or 160 acres elsewhere. Sale proceeds exempt for six months after sale.
W. Va. Code Sec. 38-10-4(a). Homestead exemption for real or personal property used as a residence; unused portion may apply to other property.
Haw. Rev. Stat. Sec. 651-92(a). Homestead exemption up to $30,000 for a head of household or a person age 65 or older.
N.H. Code Ann. Sec. 480:1. Homestead exemption for real property or manufactured housing, including the land if owned by the debtor.

Me. Rev. Stat. Ann. Sec. 4422(1). Homestead exemption up to $47,500 for an owner-occupied residence, including cooperatives; $95,000 if minor dependents reside there or if debtor is age 60+ or disabled (joint debtors may double). Sale proceeds exempt for six months.

Mont. Code Ann. Sec. 70-32-104. Homestead exemption up to $250,000 for an owner-occupied residence or mobile home; sale, condemnation, or insurance proceeds exempt for 18 months. Homestead declaration must be recorded before bankruptcy filing.
R.I. Gen. Laws Sec. 9-26-4.1. Homestead exemption for land and buildings occupied or intended to be occupied as a principal residence.
10 Del. Code Ann. Sec. 4914(c)(1). Exempts equity in real property or a manufactured home that is the debtor’s principal residence.

S.D. Cod. Laws Sec. 43-45-3. Unlimited homestead exemption for up to 160 acres in rural areas or 1 acre in urban areas. Applies to real property or mobile homes (over 240 sq. ft. and registered ≥6 months). Sale proceeds exempt up to $30,000 ($170,000 if age 70+ or widowed) for…
N.D. Cent. Code Secs. 47-18-01, 28-22-02(7). Homestead exemption for real property, house trailer, or mobile home.
Alaska Stat. Sec. 09.38.010. Principal residence up to $72,900; joint owners may each claim a portion, but the total may not exceed $72,900.
D.C. Code Sec. 15-501(a)(14). Unlimited homestead exemption for any property used as a residence, including a cooperative unit, that is occupied by the debtor or the debtor’s dependent.
Vt. Stat. Ann. Sec. 2740(19)(D). Homestead exemption for real property or mobile home, including rents, profits, and out-buildings.
Wy. Stat. Ann. § 1-20-101. Real property or house trailer you occupy.
